subject: Game Theory
title: Congestion Pricing
description: A fast breakdown of Congestion Pricing for builders.

hook.text: Every driver on a highway ignores their cost to others: one more car slows everyone. Roads are a commons.

buildup.text: Congestion pricing charges drivers more during peak hours, aligning individual costs with social costs.

discovery.text: London's congestion charge cut traffic 30% and raised £2.6B for transit. Stockholm's trial became permanent by vote.

twist.text: People hated it before it launched and loved it after. Experience changed minds. Stockholm voted 53% to keep it.

climax.text: Dynamic pricing via GPS could charge by exact route and time. Every road gets its own market-clearing price.

punchline.text: Price the road and traffic solves itself.

quiz.question: Why does congestion pricing work?
options: It makes drivers internalize the cost they impose on others
